text:
**Yes, but only some models, and only if the specs check out.** A basic power station can keep a PC running in an outage but may still interrupt it at the moment of switchover. Both Anker and EcoFlow say the same in their guides.

**What to check**
- **Documented UPS/EPS mode:** The manufacturer must state automatic switchover. Plain "pass-through charging" is not the same thing ([Anker](https://www.ankersolix.com/blogs/portable-power-station/can-a-portable-power-station-be-used-as-a-ups)).
- **Transfer time:** Look for about 10 ms or less. EcoFlow says many products advertised as UPS take 20-30 ms ([EcoFlow](https://www.ecoflow.com/us/blog/use-portable-power-station-as-ups-power-supply)). Anker notes that even 10 or 20 ms isn't 0 ms, so check your PC or NAS power supply manual ([Anker](https://www.ankersolix.com/blogs/home-power-backup/portable-power-station-ups-home-server-nas)). Many desktop power supplies tolerate brief gaps, but I'm saying that from general knowledge, not these sources.
- **Pure sine wave output:** This is preferred for computers and networking gear.
- **Enough watts and watt-hours:** Measure your PC's real draw with a plug-in watt meter. Runtime is roughly Wh × 0.85 ÷ watts. For example, 1,000 Wh at 100 W gives about 8.5 hours at best.
- **Pass-through use:** It needs to be supported for continuous plugged-in operation.

**Models with a published UPS spec in these results**
- **[Anker SOLIX S2000](https://www.ankersolix.com/blogs/portable-power-station/can-a-portable-power-station-be-used-as-a-ups):** 2,010 Wh LFP battery, 1,500 W pure sine wave output, and 10 ms UPS switchover. The page listed it at $699.99 after coupon.
- **[EcoFlow RIVER 3 Plus](https://www.ecoflow.com/us/blog/use-portable-power-station-as-ups-power-supply):** 600 W AC output and a switchover under 10 ms. That's enough for a desktop plus a drive or two. The page didn't show a price.

The links go to the manufacturers' articles on those models, since the search results didn't include direct store pages. Check the current price and the UPS spec on the product page before buying.

**Caveats**
- The BLUETTI result was only a discount-code page with no UPS or transfer-time information, so I can't say whether those models suit this use.
- If your computer or NAS manual requires 0 ms transfer, or you need voltage regulation or automatic shutdown signaling, Anker recommends a true online double-conversion UPS instead.
- A small, cheap dedicated UPS is still the simpler choice if you only need a few minutes to save work and shut down. A power station makes sense if you want hours of runtime.

If you tell me your PC's wattage and how long you want it to run, I can size it more precisely.
